source_issues.detail: src_1 (Griggs–Ho 1998) is declared READ from a URL and saved to sandbox, but no excerpt was submitted and no retrieval tool is available to me; I cannot confirm the reading. Bibliographic data for src_1–src_3 match my knowledge (Adv. Appl. Math. 21 (1998) 205–227; Math. Mag. 58 (1985) 259–271; JCTA 58 (1991) 181–197; CMJ 43 (2012) 135–140), so no sign of fabrication. Not blocking: the proof states and re-proves every step itself and cites nothing as a black box, which is exactly the use the hand-in rules permit ('a proof written out in full does, whatever its source'). src_3 is honestly marked NOT read, attribution only.

If desired, orchestrator may confirm existence/content of runs/p3_c2/sandbox/griggs_ho_cycling.pdf and .txt to validate the 'READ in full' statement and the attribution of the method to Thm. 3.7 / Lemmas 3.3–3.6. Purely for attribution accuracy; the mathematical claim does not depend on it.

computation_issues.detail: Both scripts are explicitly labelled sanity checks, not part of the proof; exact integer arithmetic; exhaustive over all partitions of the stated finite ranges (n ≤ 24; T_k for k ≤ 7 / k ≤ 8–9). Trusted re-run: code_1 exit 0 in 14.3 s (claimed 8.6 s — timing discrepancy immaterial, well under 10 min); code_2 exit 0 in 0.1 s with k=8 giving D_B=56=k²−k, consistent with the theorem. The claimed k=9 run is not in the trusted output (default argument is 8); harmless since the computation is illustrative only.

claim_provenance.notes: Formula D_B(T_k)=k²−k with explicit extremal γ_k=(k−1,k−1,k−2,…,2,1,1) as a function of k, both bounds argued in full (Parts I–III) without invoking any cited statement as a black box. The value is known in the literature (Igusa 1985, Etienne 1991; method of Griggs–Ho 1998) and this is disclosed with clear attribution, which the rules allow. Exhaustive exact computations for small k agree (trusted re-run up to k=8). Mathematical correctness of the written proof is Referee A's domain; from the evidence side nothing is missing or forbidden.

report.reproducibility_notes: Orchestrator re-ran both scripts from a clean copy: code_1 (requires code_2 in the same directory) exit 0, 14.3 s, all assertions pass for n ≤ 24 and k = 3..7; code_2 exit 0, 0.1 s, D_B(T_k)=k²−k up to k=8 observed (k=9 claimed but run with default argument 8). Both are exhaustive over their declared finite sets, use exact integer arithmetic, and are far below the 10-minute limit. Neither is needed for the proof.
